cve_candidates.description: runc container escape vulnerability allowing a malicious container or process to overwrite the host runc binary and achieve root-level code execution on the Docker host. Relevant given confirmed Docker container environment.

IPMI 2.0 RAKP authentication remote password hash retrieval. If IPMI is running, an unauthenticated attacker can retrieve HMAC-SHA1 password hashes for any valid user account via the cipher zero attack.
IKE aggressive mode PSK hash disclosure. If IKEv1 aggressive mode is enabled, pre-shared key hashes can be captured and subjected to offline brute force.
NTP trap service crash and DoS via NULL pointer dereference in ntpd. If NTP monlist is enabled, host can also be used as a DDoS amplifier.
UPnP SUBSCRIBE SSRF (CallStranger). If UPnP is running, arbitrary HTTP requests can be forged to internal services enabling SSRF, data exfiltration, and DDoS amplification.

attack_surface_summary: Target 172.19.0.3 (hostname: redteam_easy-target-1.redteam_easy_engagement-net) is a Docker container on the engagement network presenting an extremely minimal or fully blocked network surface. All 65535 TCP ports returned active RST responses — no TCP services are listening. UDP scanning produced inconsistent results across multiple passes: ports including 68 (DHCP client), 69 (TFTP), 123 (NTP), 138 (NetBIOS-DGM), 500 (IKE/ISAKMP), 520 (RIP), 623 (IPMI/RMCP), 1194 (OpenVPN), 1900 (UPnP), and 5353 (mDNS/Zeroconf) alternated between open|filtered and closed states, suggesting a dynamic stateful firewall, ICMP rate-limiting, or transient service availability. No service banners or version strings were captured. The primary attack surface is: (1) the container orchestration layer — Docker daemon misconfiguration or runc escape; (2) any UDP service that becomes reachable, particularly IPMI/623 for credential hash theft and IKE/500 for PSK disclosure; (3) the host's subnet position (172.19.0.0/16) enabling ARP spoofing and passive traffic interception; (4) lateral movement via shared Docker network bridge to sibling containers. Most promising initial-access vectors in priority order: container escape via Docker misconfiguration, UDP service exploitation if IPMI or IKE become reachable, and network-layer attacks exploiting subnet adjacency.
